elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads in full: "Customer is subject to no non-solicitation restriction under this Agreement." The prior 18-month, all-employee, solicit-or-engage covenant against Customer is gone, and no other non-solicit survives; § 12.3 is retained and reinforces that Customer gave no no-hire commitment.
Condition does not apply: no non-solicitation restriction exists after the edit, so there is no one-way covenant burdening Customer. The outcome is at least as favourable as a mutual covenant.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — the former scope ("any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term") is deleted and no restriction of any scope remains in § 12.4 or elsewhere.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — the eighteen-month post-termination period is removed entirely; no duration operates because no covenant remains.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains to which a carve-out could attach; § 12.3 separately preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied — with § 12.4 replaced by an express statement of no restriction, unsolicited approaches by Vendor personnel are unconstrained.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The "solicit or engage" language (which operated as a no-hire) is deleted; nothing prohibits Customer from hiring Vendor personnel, consistent with § 12.3's acknowledgement of no no-hire commitment.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: the sole non-solicit binding Customer (§ 12.4) is replaced with an unconditional statement that Customer is subject to no non-solicitation restriction, leaving no residual solicit/engage/no-hire mechanic.

Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because the removal of the covenant eliminates the condition each element constrains; no mutual covenant was added, which is correct for the preferred target.

Minimal: the edit is confined to the offending sentence in § 12.4. Favourable § 12.3 is retained verbatim, no survival tail, procedure, or extra obligation is added, and no words outside the target element are deleted. Replacing the sentence with a short declaratory clause rather than deleting the subsection avoids a numbering gap and adds no new requirement.

Preserves intent: no cross-references point to § 12.4, no defined term is orphaned, and the retained § 12.3 acknowledgement (no no-hire commitment) is now consistent rather than contradicted by § 12.4.

Classification as a deviation is correct — the original clause failed the fallback on every material term (one-way, 18 months from termination, all Vendor employees at any time, "engage" no-hire, no carve-outs), and the walk-away triggers (no-hire, all-personnel scope) were present.
